about: COMPLY.0 legal register: every legal and platform obligation that applies to Cerid or to products built with it, one entry per instrument and article, with its jurisdiction, official primary source and the consolidated version read, the obligation in plain words, the products, data flows and channels it applies to, the check that proves it, its effective and sunset dates, a counsel-review flag, the owning rows and the next review. scripts/check-registers.py (the crd-check-registers CTest and repository step) fails a binding obligation without an active check, a lapsed review, an entry read from no primary source when its rows close and a topic without a Turkish entry. docs/design/registers.md is the contract; it shares the standards register's format, guard and review machinery.

snapshot.method: Refreshed on 2026-11-01 by scripts/register-review.py from the approved source plan (86 records; report docs/sessions/2026-11-01-legal-register-first-read.md).

review.cadence: A light scan quarterly, after each yearly platform event (the April SDK rule, Google I/O, WWDC, the August target API rule) and after each dated effective day the register holds, and a full re-research every year or when a scan finds a pinned instrument amended; Official Gazette of Turkey, EUR-Lex and Steamworks announcements are recorded as runs with their triggering entries. Reviews propose ROADMAP amendments for the user and never edit rows.

entries.title: KVKK: processing conditions and special categories

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Process personal data only lawfully, for specified purposes, minimised and kept no longer than needed, on a condition of Article 5 (explicit consent or a listed ground) and the stricter Article 6 rules for special categories; delete, destroy or anonymise it when the purpose ends.

check.name: data inventory CTest: every flow declares its lawful basis per jurisdiction

entries.title: KVKK: the aydınlatma notice kept separate from explicit consent

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Inform the data subject (aydınlatma) when data is collected, in a notice separate from any request for explicit consent; consent is specific, informed and freely given and is never bundled with the notice or a service condition.

entries.title: KVKK: data subject rights and the 30-day answer

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Answer access, correction, deletion and objection requests within 30 days at the latest, free of charge (a fee on the Board's tariff only where answering has its own cost), accepting or refusing each with reasons in writing or electronically; deletion reaches every store and backup window.

check.name: data subject request service tests (deletion reaches every store)

entries.title: KVKK: data security and breach notification to the Board

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Take the technical and administrative measures that keep personal data secure; notify the data subject and the Board of a breach as soon as possible (the Board set 72 hours).

check.name: breach-notification runbook rehearsal with per-regulator clocks

entries.title: KVKK: transfer abroad after Law No. 7499 and the 2024 By-Law

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 Article 9 as amended by Law No. 7499, and the By-Law on the Procedures and Principles for the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad

entries.obligation: Transfer personal data abroad only on an adequacy decision, an appropriate safeguard (standard contracts notified to the Authority within five business days and used unmodified, binding corporate rules) or an incidental case; record each transfer and its mechanism.

check.name: transfer records CTest with standard-contract notification reminders

entries.title: KVKK: VERBIS registration of the data controller

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Register the publisher in the Data Controllers Registry (VERBIS) when the Board's thresholds or the foreign controller rule require it, before processing starts.

entries.title: KVKK: the regulation on deletion, destruction and anonymisation

instrument.name: Regulation on the Deletion, Destruction or Anonymisation of Personal Data

entries.obligation: Keep a retention and destruction policy, destroy personal data at the first periodic destruction after its purpose ends (at most every six months) and keep destruction records for three years.

check.name: retention CTest: a flow outliving its retention fails

entries.title: Turkish Penal Code: personal data offences
entries.obligation: Never record personal data unlawfully (Article 135, half as much again for the special categories), give, disseminate or obtain it unlawfully (Article 136) or fail to destroy it when the legal periods end (Article 138); a company gets the security measures of Article 140, so the data inventory and deletion service make every processing step lawful and auditable.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Law No. 7545: incident and vulnerability reporting
entries.obligation: Report the vulnerabilities and cyber incidents found in the services a product offers to the Cybersecurity Presidency without delay, hand over the data and documents it requests in time, take the measures the legislation sets and keep systems, software and records open to its audits.

check.name: reporting workflow rehearsed against seeded incidents

entries.title: Cybersecurity Law No. 7545: permits for cybersecurity products
entries.obligation: Obtain the Cybersecurity Presidency's approval before operating as a cybersecurity company subject to certification or authorisation, and before exporting a cybersecurity product, system or service its procedures make subject to permit; notify it of a merger, division or share transfer of a company producing them, which needs its approval where control changes; classify every Cerid product against that definition first.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: Turkish Penal Code: information-system offences
entries.obligation: The coordinated disclosure policy and its researcher safe harbour respect the offences of unauthorised access or remaining in a system and unlawful monitoring of its data transfers (Article 243), hindering or disrupting a system and altering, deleting or inserting its data (Article 244) and making, selling or holding a device, program or code made exclusively for these offences (Article 245/A); Cerid never asks a researcher to commit one, and its security tools are not made exclusively for them.

entries.title: Electronic Communications Law No. 5809: BTK encryption rules

instrument.name: Electronic Communications Law No. 5809 and the BTK rules on coded and encrypted communication
instrument.article: Article 39 and the BTK rules on coded and encrypted communication

entries.obligation: Classify encryption in communication products against Article 39, under which the BTK sets the procedure for coded or encrypted communication within an electronic communication service (breaching it is an offence, Article 63(6)), and meet any notification or authorisation duty its rules set, without key escrow or weakened end-to-end encryption.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: Ministry of Trade dual-use export rules

instrument.name: Ministry of Trade communiqué on the export of dual-use and sensitive goods

entries.obligation: Identify the current communiqué and classify each export against its Category 5 Part 2 list.

check.name: classification record per product and release

entries.note: The instrument and its effective date are identified on the first primary read; it is then pinned.

entries.title: Turkey's asset-freeze regime

instrument.name: Law No. 6415 on the Prevention of the Financing of Terrorism and Law No. 7262 on preventing the financing of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction
instrument.article: Law No. 6415 Articles 5-7, 11-13 and 15; Law No. 7262's proliferation freezes

entries.obligation: Screen distribution, accounts and payments against Turkey's asset-freeze decisions: the President's decisions implementing the UN Security Council lists (Article 5), foreign states' requests (Article 6) and domestic freezes (Article 7), each binding on its publication in the Official Gazette (Articles 11-12); make no transaction for a designated person and facilitate none (Article 13), report receivables and debts toward one to MASAK within 30 days (Article 12(3)), and never provide funds or financial services to one (Article 15).

check.name: crd-comply-tests [sanctions]: parties and destinations screened against each authority's list, failing closed on a missing or stale list

entries.title: Law No. 5651: content, hosting and social network provider duties

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet

entries.obligation: Act on removal and access-blocking orders within the legal deadlines, keep the provider records the law requires and meet the social network provider duties when a product reaches their thresholds.

entries.title: Law No. 5651: game-platform duties

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: A game platform (infrastructure that exhibits, sells, distributes or runs digital games, manages licences or connects users) offers no game without its due age rating (an unrated game only at the highest age criterion) and removes unrated content, gives parents clear tools that control account settings and approve paid transactions, and gives the Authority the explanations it requests at once and within the period it sets of at most 15 days; a foreign-based platform above 100,000 daily accesses from Turkey also appoints and publishes a representative in Turkey.

check.name: 5651 game-platform kit CTests (parental payment approval, representative threshold monitoring)

entries.title: Law No. 5651: age ratings on game platforms

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: Offer no game without its due age rating (an unrated game only at the highest age criterion) and produce the Turkish rating under the by-law the Authority issues on the rating criteria.

check.name: rating answers authored once generate every submission

entries.title: ICTA secondary rules for game platforms

instrument.name: ICTA (BTK) regulation under Law No. 5651 for game platforms

entries.obligation: Track the secondary rules ICTA issues for game platforms and pin them when published.

entries.title: Law No. 5651: the under-15 restriction on social networks

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: Where a product meets the social network provider definition, serve no child under 15 (with age verification), serve children of 15 and over a separate service, publish the measures taken, give parents clear tools over account settings, paid transactions and usage time, and block deceptive advertising.

entries.title: Law No. 5809: authorisation for communication services

instrument.name: Electronic Communications Law No. 5809 and the BTK authorisation regulation

entries.obligation: Classify each communication product (voice, video, text) as an electronic communication service or not and, where it is one, notify the BTK before operating it in Turkey, with a usage right where it needs numbers or frequencies (Article 9; operating without notification is an offence, Article 63(1)), under the BTK authorisation regulation.

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.title: BTK rules on personal data in electronic communications

instrument.name: BTK regulation on processing and protecting personal data in the electronic communications sector

entries.obligation: Apply the sector rules on traffic and location data, retention and security to communication products operated in Turkey.

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.note: In force when the research read it on 2026-10-27; the version date is confirmed on the first primary read.

entries.title: Law No. 6112 and RTÜK internet broadcasting rules

instrument.name: Law No. 6112 on Radio and Television Broadcasting and RTÜK's internet broadcasting regulation

entries.obligation: Classify live streaming against Article 29/A before offering it in Turkey: a media service provider offering radio, television or on-demand services only on the internet needs an RTÜK broadcast licence and a platform operator transmitting them a transmission authorisation, while individual communication, platforms not dedicated to transmitting such services and pure hosts are outside it (29/A(4)); the joint RTÜK and BTK regulation sets the procedure.

entries.title: Law No. 6563: commercial electronic messages and IYS

instrument.name: Law No. 6563 on the Regulation of Electronic Commerce

entries.obligation: Send commercial electronic messages only with the recipient's prior consent, written or electronic (Article 6), recorded in the message management system (IYS), where a consent not transferred is invalid (Article 11(5)); each message matches its consent and identifies the sender with its contact details (Article 7), and carries an easy, free opt-out honoured within three business days (Article 8).

check.name: consent records CTest for commercial messages

entries.title: Law No. 6563: ETBIS registration

instrument.name: Law No. 6563 on the Regulation of Electronic Commerce and its intermediary service provider regulation
instrument.article: Articles 2(1)(ı) and 11(4); the regulation on service providers and intermediary service providers

entries.obligation: Register the store and its sellers in the e-commerce information system (ETBIS) before trading.

entries.title: Law No. 6502 and the Distance Contracts Regulation

instrument.name: Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 and the Regulation on Distance Contracts
instrument.article: Article 48; the Regulation on Distance Contracts

entries.obligation: Give the pre-contract information the regulation lists and say that confirming the order creates a payment duty (the burden of proof is the seller's), confirm the contract on a durable medium and honour the fourteen-day withdrawal right (Article 48(4): extended up to a year when its information was missing), with the regulation's lawful waiver for digital content delivered at once; a marketplace intermediary shares the seller's liability for the pre-contract information and its records (Article 48(6)).

check.name: checkout flow tests over the pre-contract steps

entries.title: Law No. 5070 on electronic signatures
entries.obligation: Where a contract, invoice or developer agreement needs a written form, use a secure electronic signature (made with a secure signature-creation device on a qualified electronic certificate, Article 4), which Article 5 gives the legal effect of a handwritten one; a transaction the law subjects to an official form or ceremony, and a guarantee contract other than a bank letter of guarantee or a surety bond of an insurer established in Turkey, cannot be made with it.

entries.title: Law No. 5846: software as a work and licence form

instrument.name: Law No. 5846 on Intellectual and Artistic Works

entries.obligation: Treat software (with its preparatory design) and assets as works, though the ideas and principles under a program and its interfaces are not (Article 2); an employee's work made on duty is exercised by the employer unless a contract says otherwise (Article 18); licences and transfers are written and name each right granted (Article 52), a licensee passes a right on only with the author's written consent (Article 49), and third-party works are used only within their licence.

check.name: licence-policy CTest over every pin and package

entries.title: Industrial Property Law No. 6769
entries.obligation: Clear product names against registered trademarks, whose holder can stop an identical or confusingly similar sign on the same or similar goods and services and the unfair use of a well-known mark (Articles 7 and 29), and respect patents before release, including codec patents: a computer program as such is no invention, but a patented product or process is used only with the holder's consent (Articles 82(2)(c) and 85).

entries.title: Trademark filings for product names (TURKPATENT, EUIPO)

instrument.name: Industrial Property Law No. 6769
instrument.article: Articles 7(1), 11 and 23; EUIPO filings under Regulation (EU) 2017/1001

entries.obligation: File trademarks for product names with TURKPATENT (protection comes only by registration, Article 7(1); one mark per application with its goods and services list, Article 11; ten years from the application, renewed in the six months before the term ends, Article 23) and with the EUIPO before launch.

entries.title: Law No. 5378 on Persons with Disabilities

instrument.name: Law No. 5378 on Persons with Disabilities

entries.obligation: Make information services and information and communication technology accessible to persons with disabilities (Article 7) against the TSE accessibility standards (Article 3(1)(g)), and make the reasonable accommodations that keep storefronts and purchase flows free of discrimination (Article 4/A).

entries.title: VAT Law No. 3065 for digital sales
entries.obligation: Charge and declare VAT on store sales of goods and services performed or used in Turkey (Articles 1 and 6), at the rate the President sets under Article 28; as a provider without a residence, office or seat in Turkey selling electronic services to natural persons not registered for VAT, declare and pay it itself (Article 9(1), from 1 January 2018) under the Ministry's scope and procedure (the VAT No. 3 return).

check.name: tax calculation tests per sale type

entries.title: Digital service tax (Law No. 7194)

instrument.name: Law No. 7194 on the Digital Service Tax

entries.obligation: Monitor the thresholds (exempt while the previous year's revenue from in-scope services was below TRY 20 million in Turkey or EUR 750 million worldwide, counted for the consolidated group, Article 4) and declare the tax monthly, by the end of the following month (Article 6), on revenue from digital content sales including games and in-game purchases, platforms where users interact and intermediation (Article 1), at the rate in force: Article 5 sets 7.5 % and Decision No. 10767 (Official Gazette of 25 December 2025, No. 33118) 5 % from 2026 and 2.5 % from 2027.

entries.title: Tax Procedure Law No. 213: e-invoice and e-archive

instrument.name: Tax Procedure Law No. 213 and the e-invoice and e-archive general communiqués

entries.obligation: Issue e-archive or e-invoices for every store sale and keep them for the statutory period.

entries.title: Law No. 6493 on payment services

instrument.name: Law No. 6493 on Payment and Security Settlement Systems, Payment Services and Electronic Money Institutions

entries.obligation: Collect payments only through a bank or a payment or electronic money institution licensed by the Central Bank (Articles 13(2), 14 and 18; acting without a licence is an offence, Article 28) and decide the merchant-of-record role so the store never provides an unlicensed payment service; a store credit or wallet usable only in the store's own network stays outside the law until the Central Bank brings it in by volume (Articles 12(2)(h) and 18(5)).

check.name: payment adapter tests against a licensed institution's sandbox

entries.title: KVKK recommendations on personal data in artificial intelligence

instrument.name: KVKK recommendations on the protection of personal data in the field of artificial intelligence

entries.obligation: Apply privacy by design, minimisation and impact assessment to AI features that process personal data.

entries.title: Turkey's artificial intelligence bill
entries.obligation: Track the bill and pin its duties once enacted.

entries.title: GDPR: principles, lawful basis, privacy by design and records
entries.obligation: Process personal data lawfully on an Article 6 basis (Article 9 for special categories), minimised and purpose-bound, with data protection by design and by default and a record of processing activities.

check.name: data inventory CTest: every flow declares its lawful basis per jurisdiction

entries.title: GDPR: children's consent
entries.obligation: Where consent is the basis for an information society service offered to a child, obtain the holder of parental responsibility's consent below the member state's age (13 to 16) with reasonable verification.

entries.title: GDPR: transparency and data subject rights
entries.obligation: Give transparent notices and honour access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection within one month.

check.name: data subject request service tests (deletion reaches every store)

entries.title: GDPR: security and 72-hour breach notification
entries.obligation: Secure processing appropriately and notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach, and the data subjects when the risk is high.

check.name: breach-notification runbook rehearsal with per-regulator clocks

entries.title: GDPR: data protection impact assessments
entries.obligation: Assess high-risk processing (crash pools with memory contents, anti-cheat signals, children's data) before it starts.

entries.title: GDPR: transfers to third countries
entries.obligation: Transfer personal data outside the EEA only on an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, recorded per flow, and choose server regions accordingly.

entries.title: EDPB Guidelines 01/2025 on pseudonymisation
entries.obligation: Pseudonymise crash and telemetry identifiers with keyed one-way functions whose keys stay separate; pseudonymised data remains personal data.

entries.title: ePrivacy Directive: storing and reading on devices
entries.obligation: Store or read identifiers on a user's device only with consent unless strictly necessary for the service the user asked for.

entries.title: CRA: reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
entries.obligation: Through ENISA's single reporting platform, notify the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA at once of every actively exploited vulnerability and severe incident in a product with digital elements on the EU market: an early warning within 24 hours, a notification within 72 hours and a final report (14 days after a corrective measure for a vulnerability, one month after the notification for an incident).

check.name: reporting workflow rehearsed against seeded incidents

entries.title: CRA: essential requirements, support period and SBOM
entries.obligation: Meet the essential cybersecurity requirements, declare a support period, keep an SBOM, handle vulnerabilities with coordinated disclosure and ship security updates for every product with digital elements.

check.name: release CTests: SBOM, declared support period and reporting contact

entries.title: CRA: reporting contact and ENISA platform account
entries.obligation: Hold the account on ENISA's single reporting platform the Article 14 notifications go through before 11 September 2026, and designate the single point of contact users report vulnerabilities to, easily identifiable, named in the user information and not limited to automated tools (Article 13(17), applying from 11 December 2027).

entries.title: NIS2 for services Cerid operates
entries.obligation: If an operated service (store, servers, crash pool) falls in scope, apply the risk-management measures and the 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month incident reporting.

check.name: scope classification record and incident runbook rehearsal

entries.title: Product Liability Directive: software as a product
entries.obligation: Software is a product; a missing security update can make it defective and liability cannot be excluded by contract, so support periods and update delivery are evidence-backed.

check.name: support-period and update-delivery records per product

entries.title: AI Act: transparency for AI interaction and synthetic media
entries.obligation: Tell people when they interact with an AI system and mark synthetic audio, image, video and text in a machine-readable way (C2PA content credentials); systems already on the market are marked by 2026-12-02.

check.name: AI feature CTests: disclosure and marking present

entries.title: AI Act: prohibited practices and AI literacy
entries.obligation: Never place a prohibited AI practice in a product and ensure AI literacy of the people operating AI features.

entries.title: AI Act: general-purpose model obligations
entries.obligation: If Cerid ships or fine-tunes a general-purpose model, keep its documentation, copyright policy and training data summary.
entries.note: Pinned when AI.1 decides that Cerid ships or fine-tunes a general-purpose model.

entries.title: Digital Services Act: notice and action and protection of minors
entries.obligation: Hosting and platform features take notices, issue statements of reasons, handle complaints and protect minors (Article 28); the micro and small enterprise exemption covers only the platform-tier duties.

entries.title: Copyright DSM Directive: text and data mining and Article 17

instrument.name: Directive (EU) 2019/790 (Copyright in the Digital Single Market)

entries.obligation: Respect text and data mining opt-outs for training data and meet Article 17 for content-sharing services.

entries.title: European Accessibility Act
entries.obligation: E-commerce services (storefronts, purchase flows) and electronic communications with real-time text meet the accessibility requirements (EN 301 549, WCAG 2.2 AA) with an accessibility statement.

entries.title: EU dual-use regulation: cryptography

instrument.name: Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (dual-use items)
instrument.article: Annex I Category 5 Part 2 and the cryptography note

entries.obligation: Classify every export's cryptography against Category 5 Part 2 and its cryptography note and hold the record.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: EU restrictive measures

instrument.name: Council regulations adopted under Article 215 TFEU (EU sanctions)

entries.obligation: Screen distribution, accounts and payments against the EU sanctions lists.

check.name: crd-comply-tests [sanctions]: parties and destinations screened against each authority's list, failing closed on a missing or stale list

entries.note: The lists change continuously; the screening reads the current list at use.

entries.title: CPC key principles on in-game virtual currencies

instrument.name: Consumer Protection Cooperation network key principles on in-game virtual currencies

entries.obligation: Price virtual currency items in real money as well, never obscure costs or pressure minors, and disclose paid random item odds.

check.name: loot-box and virtual-currency rule engine tests

entries.title: Consumer Rights Directive: digital content and withdrawal
entries.obligation: Give pre-contract information and honour the 14-day withdrawal right, with the express-consent waiver for digital content supplied at once.

check.name: checkout flow tests over the pre-contract steps

entries.title: Digital Fairness Act
entries.obligation: Track the proposal (dark patterns, addictive design, virtual currencies) and pin its duties once adopted.

entries.title: European Electronic Communications Code
entries.obligation: Classify voice, video and text features as number-independent interpersonal communication services and meet the duties that follow.

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.title: Audiovisual Media Services Directive for video sharing and live streaming
entries.obligation: Classify video-sharing and live-streaming features and apply the video-sharing platform duties (minors, reporting, terms) where they apply.

entries.title: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018

instrument.name: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018

entries.obligation: Meet the UK GDPR's principles, rights, breach and transfer duties for UK users, as the GDPR entries do for the EU.

entries.title: Age Appropriate Design Code
entries.obligation: Design services likely to be accessed by children with high-privacy defaults, minimised data and no nudging.

check.name: privacy default tests for child accounts

entries.title: Online Safety Act 2023

instrument.name: Online Safety Act 2023 and Ofcom's codes

entries.obligation: In-game chat, voice and user content assess illegal-harm and children's risks, offer reporting and blocking, and use age assurance where children's access duties apply.

check.name: chat and voice safety hook CTests

entries.title: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022

instrument.name: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 and its regulations

entries.obligation: Connectable products ban universal default passwords, publish a vulnerability reporting policy and state the minimum security update period.

check.name: release CTests: reporting contact and support period

entries.title: Equality Act 2010
entries.obligation: Make reasonable adjustments so disabled users can use services, storefronts and purchase flows.

entries.title: UK sanctions (the UK Sanctions List)
entries.obligation: Screen distribution, accounts and payments against the UK Sanctions List.

check.name: crd-comply-tests [sanctions]: parties and destinations screened against each authority's list, failing closed on a missing or stale list

entries.title: COPPA Rule as amended in 2025
entries.obligation: Services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting their data give notice, obtain verifiable parental consent, minimise and retain data only as long as needed, and keep a written security programme.

entries.title: EAR: encryption classification and License Exception ENC
entries.obligation: Classify every export's cryptography (5D002 or mass-market 5D992.c), apply License Exception ENC with its self-classification where it applies, and give stores the export-compliance answer the record supports.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: EAR: annual self-classification report

instrument.name: Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR 730-774)
instrument.article: Section 740.17(b)(1) and (e)(3) and Supplement No. 8 to Part 742

entries.obligation: File the self-classification report (Supplement No. 8 to Part 742) by 1 February for the previous calendar year's exports of items exported under Section 740.17(b)(1) that stay in 5A002, 5B002 or 5D002 and of mass-market components and executable software in 5A992 or 5D992; mass-market end items are not reported.

entries.title: US sanctions (OFAC)

instrument.name: International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the OFAC regulations

entries.obligation: Screen distribution, accounts and payments against the OFAC lists and embargoed destinations.

check.name: crd-comply-tests [sanctions]: parties and destinations screened against each authority's list, failing closed on a missing or stale list

entries.title: CCPA as amended by the CPRA
entries.obligation: Give notice at collection, honour know, delete, correct and opt-out (sale or sharing) requests and limit sensitive data use; the other US state laws join as their own entries when a product enters their markets.

entries.title: Section 508 standards
entries.obligation: Engineering products sold to US federal bodies meet the 508 standards (WCAG 2.0 AA by reference).
entries.note: Pinned when a product is offered to a US federal body.

entries.title: Americans with Disabilities Act, Title III
entries.obligation: Public accommodations, including online storefronts as US courts and the Department of Justice apply them, are accessible.

entries.title: CVAA: accessible advanced communications services

instrument.name: Twenty-First Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act rules

entries.obligation: Voice, video and text chat in games and products is accessible to people with disabilities.

entries.title: Secure software development attestation

instrument.name: CISA secure software development attestation form (NIST SP 800-218)

entries.obligation: Attest secure development practices when selling software to US federal agencies.
entries.note: Pinned when a product is sold to a US federal agency.

entries.title: DMCA notice and takedown
entries.obligation: Hosted user content keeps a designated agent, acts on notices and counter-notices and terminates repeat infringers.

entries.title: Texas App Store Accountability Act
entries.obligation: Track the enjoined law (age verification and parental consent through app stores) and pin it if it takes effect.

entries.title: Utah App Store Accountability Act
entries.obligation: Track the law's app store age verification and parental consent duties and pin them for a store serving Utah.

entries.title: Brazil LGPD

instrument.name: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (Law No. 13.709/2018)

entries.obligation: Process Brazilian users' data on a legal basis with the principles, rights and breach duties of the law.

entries.title: Brazil ECA Digital
entries.obligation: Protect children in digital products: age verification, parental supervision tools and no paid random items for minors.

check.name: loot-box rule engine and parental-tool tests

entries.title: China PIPL
entries.obligation: Process personal information of users in China on a legal basis, meet the localisation and cross-border assessment duties.
entries.note: Pinned when a product enters China.

entries.title: China synthetic content labelling measures

instrument.name: Measures for labelling AI-generated synthetic content

entries.obligation: Label generated content explicitly and implicitly for products in China.

check.name: AI feature CTests: disclosure and marking present

entries.note: Pinned when a product enters China.

entries.title: China commercial cryptography import and export controls

instrument.name: Cryptography Law of the People's Republic of China and the Commercial Cryptography Administration Regulations
instrument.article: Cryptography Law Article 28; the Regulations' import licensing, export control and product certification provisions

questions.question: For each data flow Cerid products run (crash reports, telemetry, network identity, anti-cheat signals, accounts, payments, user content and communications), which processing condition of Article 5 of Law No. 6698 may the publisher rely on, which flows need explicit consent, and does any of them process special categories of personal data under Article 6 (for example voice recordings, or anti-cheat signals that could reveal health or biometric data)?

Does a layered in-product notice shown before the first upload, with explicit consent asked in a separate step and a refusal leaving the product fully usable, meet Articles 3, 5 and 10 of Law No. 6698 and the communiqué on the obligation to inform, and which items must the first layer of the notice carry?

Which technical and administrative measures does the Board expect under Article 12 of Law No. 6698 for crash dumps that may hold memory contents, and from which moment does the 72-hour breach notification run when a processor (the cloud host) detects the breach?

Which mechanism of Article 9 of Law No. 6698, as amended by Law No. 7499, covers transfers to the cloud regions outside Turkey that the crash pool, accounts and store use, which standard contract applies when the publisher is the controller and the cloud host its processor, and what must the notification to the Authority within five business days contain?

Is the publisher exempt from VERBIS registration under the Board's thresholds (employees and annual balance sheet total) when its main activity includes processing players' personal data, and by when must it register relative to the first release that sends data off a machine?

Which reporting duties of Cybersecurity Law No. 7545 and its secondary rules apply to a software publisher that operates no critical infrastructure, to whom and within what time must a vulnerability or incident in a released product or an operated service (the store, game servers, the crash pool) be reported, and do they cover vulnerabilities that third parties report to the publisher?

Does any Cerid export (the engine package, its tools and the products built on it) meet the definition of a cybersecurity product or service in Law No. 7545, in particular an engine that verifies signed configuration, a sandbox that isolates untrusted code or an anti-cheat component, and if so which permit, certification or export authorisation does it need?

Does a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy whose safe harbour covers only the publisher's own products and test environments protect researchers and the publisher under Articles 243 to 245 of the Turkish Penal Code No. 5237, and what wording must the policy use?

Do the BTK encryption rules under Electronic Communications Law No. 5809 set any notification, authorisation or key-disclosure duty for end-to-end encrypted voice, video and text inside games and collaborative products distributed or operated in Turkey, and do they allow TLS 1.3 and QUIC with the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange without key escrow?

Which Ministry of Trade communiqué currently lists the dual-use goods subject to export control from Turkey, does its Category 5 Part 2 list with the cryptography note follow the Wassenaar Dual-Use List, and does making software available for download from Turkey count as an export under it?

Which roles of Law No. 5651 (content provider, hosting provider, access provider or social network provider) does the publisher take for user content in games, the store and mod hubs, and which deadlines and record-keeping duties follow from each role?

Do the 2026 game-platform provisions of Law No. 5651 (Additional Article 5, added by Law No. 7578) apply to a storefront or launcher that sells only the publisher's own games, or only to platforms that also offer third-party games; which authority do they refer to as the Authority once Law No. 7590 moved the law's other provisions from the ICTA to the Cybersecurity Presidency; how are the 100,000 daily accesses from Turkey counted; and what must the record of a parent's approval of a paid transaction hold?

Does a game with in-game chat, friend lists or user-generated content meet the social network provider definition of Law No. 5651 as amended in 2026, and which age signal meets the duty to keep children under 15 from accounts?

Do voice, video and text features carried over the internet inside a game or collaborative product, with no telephone numbers and no network the publisher operates, need a BTK authorisation under Articles 9 and 10 of Law No. 5809 and the authorisation regulation?

Does the BTK regulation on processing and protecting personal data in the electronic communications sector apply to an over-the-top communication feature of a game or collaborative product that needs no BTK authorisation, and if so which retention and localisation rules follow?

Does a live stream of gameplay or of a collaborative session offered through a Cerid product to viewers in Turkey need an RTÜK internet broadcasting licence under Article 29/A of Law No. 6112, and does the answer change when users, not the publisher, broadcast?

For digital content delivered at once after purchase, which express consent and acknowledgement wording lawfully ends the right of withdrawal under the Regulation on Distance Contracts, and what must the confirmation on a durable medium contain?

Which form must licences and assignments of rights in software and assets take under Articles 48 to 52 of Law No. 5846 (written, each right named) for contributors, contractors and purchased assets, and does a click-through end-user licence meet it?

Which trademark clearance searches (TURKPATENT, EUIPO, WIPO Madrid) are enough before a product is named, and do the patents on the media codecs Cerid decodes need licences for distribution in Turkey?

Does the publisher, a Turkish company selling digital games and items to consumers in Turkey, fall under the ordinary VAT regime of Law No. 3065, and when does the VAT-3 regime for electronic services by non-residents apply to sales the store makes for foreign developers?

Does the store's revenue from third-party games, in-game items or subscriptions fall within the digital services of Law No. 7194, how are the worldwide and Turkish revenue thresholds measured for a group, and which rate applies for 2026 and 2027?
Which e-archive or e-invoice duties apply to each store sale to consumers and to businesses, from which revenue threshold, and for how long and where must the electronic records be kept?

Does the store collecting payments for third-party developers' games and paying the developers make the publisher a payment service provider under Law No. 6493, or does a merchant-of-record model (the publisher sells as the seller and buys from the developers) avoid the licence?

Which legal basis of Article 6 GDPR (legitimate interests after a balancing test, or consent) may the publisher rely on for crash reports, telemetry and anti-cheat signals of users in the Union, and does any of them process data of the categories of Article 9?

Do crash pools that may hold memory contents, anti-cheat signals and children's data each need a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 GDPR and the supervisory authorities' lists, and must the publisher consult an authority before the processing starts?

Which transfer tool of Chapter V GDPR lets personal data of users in the Union reach a publisher established in Turkey (which has no adequacy decision), which module of the standard contractual clauses applies, and must the publisher appoint a representative in the Union under Article 27?

Do the store, the game servers or the crash pool bring the publisher, established outside the Union, into the scope of Directive (EU) 2022/2555 in any member state (for example as an online marketplace or a cloud or data centre provider), and if so under which member state's law?

For how long must security updates be provided so that software placed on the market in the Union is not defective under Directive (EU) 2024/2853, and is the publisher, a manufacturer established outside the Union, liable directly or through an importer or authorised representative?

If Cerid fine-tunes or distributes an open-weight general-purpose model in its agent features, does the publisher become a provider of a general-purpose AI model under Articles 53 to 55 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, and does the exemption for models released under a free and open-source licence apply?

Which tier of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (hosting service, online platform or marketplace) do in-game user content, mod hubs and the store each fall under, does the micro and small enterprise exemption apply, and must the publisher, established outside the Union, designate a legal representative under Article 13?

Does a machine-readable reservation of text and data mining rights under Article 4 of Directive (EU) 2019/790 bind the publisher's training of agent models, and is a mod hub where users upload works an online content-sharing service provider under Article 17?

Does Regulation (EU) 2021/821 reach the publisher when its software is downloaded from servers in the Union, and is each export's classification against Annex I Category 5 Part 2 and the cryptography note correct, in particular that cryptography limited to authentication and integrity is not controlled?

Are voice, video and text features inside games and collaborative products number-independent interpersonal communication services under Directive (EU) 2018/1972, or minor ancillary features that recital 17 excludes, and which duties follow if they are services?

Is a feature that lets users share gameplay videos or live streams a video-sharing platform service under Directive 2010/13/EU as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/1808, or an ancillary feature outside it, and which member state's law applies to a publisher established outside the Union?

Must the publisher appoint a representative in the United Kingdom under Article 27 UK GDPR, which transfer tool covers personal data of UK users sent to Turkey (the International Data Transfer Agreement or the Addendum to the EU clauses), and do the answers for the GDPR otherwise apply unchanged?

Do in-game chat, voice and user content make a product a regulated user-to-user service under the Online Safety Act 2023, is it likely to be accessed by children, and which measures of Ofcom's codes and which age assurance does that require?

Does the EAR reach the publisher's software at all (a Turkish company, no US-origin encryption content, but downloads served from US servers such as a store's), and where it does, is mass-market 5D992.c under section 740.17(b)(1) the right classification for an export that performs confidentiality, and is the annual self-classification report then owed?

Does the publisher meet a threshold of the CCPA as amended by the CPRA for users in California (annual revenue, consumers whose data it buys, sells or shares, or revenue share from selling or sharing), and does sending crash reports or telemetry to a service provider count as selling or sharing?

Do the US courts that matter treat an online store or a game launcher as a place of public accommodation under Title III of the ADA, and against which technical standard (WCAG 2.2 level AA) should its accessibility be measured?

Do the duties of Law No. 15.211/2025 (age verification, parental supervision, no paid random items for minors) apply to a foreign publisher's games and store offered in Brazil, from which day, and which age verification methods meet them?

If a product enters China, must the publisher designate a representative under Article 53 of the Personal Information Protection Law, which cross-border route (security assessment, standard contract or certification) applies to crash reports and accounts, and must the data stay in China?

If a product that uses TLS 1.3 and QUIC with internationally standard algorithms enters China, does it need an import licence, export control or commercial cryptography product certification under the Cryptography Law and the 2023 Commercial Cryptography Administration Regulations, or does the treatment of mass-market consumer products cover it?

Raw files stay outside the repository, re-fetched and verified by digest.
